Public Portion 
 1. Amended Ordinance Chapter 16 Article V - Youth Commission (06/01/2026) 
 
Minutes: 
On September 18, 2026, the General Government Committee, chaired by Councilor Justin Hurst, 
met virtually at 12:01 p.m. to review the proposed Youth Commission ordinance. Councilor 
Kateri Walsh participated in the meeting. Commissioner Helen Caulton-Harris and Shenell Ford 
of the Department of Health and Human Services also participated. 
 
The committee reviewed revisions requested during the prior meeting. The revised ordinance 
includes the City Council President or a designated representative and provides for the City 
Council to appoint three Youth Commission members. The proposed Commission would provide 
Springfield youth with a formal role in identifying and discussing issues affecting young people, 
including mental health, social media, food insecurity, public safety, healthy relationships, 
financial literacy, civic engagement, school safety, and other matters identified by youth 
members. 
The committee discussed the anticipated selection and participation process. The committee is 
developing selection criteria, and representatives of the Mayor and City Council are expected to 
coordinate on a consistent process. The Youth Commission is also expected to provide quarterly 
reports to the City Council regarding its work. 
The discussion included the importance of youth participation in City government and the
addition of City Council representation to the revised ordinance. Because a quorum of committee 
members was not present, the committee did not take a formal vote to advance the ordinance. 
Chair Hurst stated that the ordinance was expected to proceed to the full City Council for 
second- and third-step consideration at an upcoming meeting. The revised Youth Commission 
ordinance was the document reviewed. 
Meeting adjourned: approximately 12:11 p.m.
